edge_explainer: NOT the WO&O/TUYA class, and the court's central finding is that the SCREEN WAS WRONG TWICE, both times against the stock. (1) THE SHELF'S OWN IN-RUN CORRECTION IS REFUTED. It cut net cash from +0.66 to +0.24 on the grounds that 57% of 'cash' was short-term INVESTMENTS. The company's accounting policy says otherwise: 'Fixed term deposits include cash balances held on medium to long term fixed term contracts of more than 3 months for investment purposes'; treasury note: 'Surplus cash... is held in a variety of 3-12 month deposits with NatWest and Lloyds Bank'; instruments note: deposits held 'for between 6 and 12 months', earning 4.52%, 100% GBP at 30-Sep-25. H1 cash flow confirms: 'Cash placed on fixed term deposit (18,000)' / 'Fixed term deposits maturing 22,000'. This is UK clearing-bank cash on an IAS 7 MATURITY technicality — the polar opposite of CAPD's $99.8m of listed junior-miner equities at FVTPL, the shape guard (o) was built for. The group's ENTIRE market-risk securities book is GBP 236k. Honest net cash = GBP 29.06m incl. leases = 67.6% of cap. (2) 'EBIT NEGATIVE / MELTING' IS A STATUTORY-PLUS-SEASONAL ARTIFACT. Adjusted EBIT FY25 = +GBP 2,214k, UP 29%; statutory operating loss only (GBP 391k). H1 is structurally the loss-making half (H1 FY25 adj EBIT -372k vs full-year +2,214k), and the screen scored a 31-Mar balance-sheet date. Management confirms: 'The Board expects trading to be weighted towards the rest of FY26'; the year-end was changed precisely because revenues are 'weighted toward the final third of the calendar year'. Any TTM annualisation of OMG is wrong by construction. (3) THE TUYA BAR IS PASSED, FOUR WAYS: a GBP 10m buyback ran 2024-10-11 to 2026-05-21 and CANCELLED 19,505,301 shares = 14.8% of opening capital (cancelled, not treasury); dividends GBP 4.2m FY25 + GBP 3.7m H1 FY26; FY25 prelims state 'GBP 12.5m returned to shareholders through buybacks and dividends'; broker corporate-action data independently confirms 3.25p ex-2026-02-12 paid 2026-03-27 and 3.25p ex-2024-12-12 paid 2025-03-05. ~GBP 17.5m returned in under two years = ~41% of today's market cap. (4) BLEED BOUNDED AND SMALL: cash+deposits 50.7 (Sep-24) -> 37.3 (Sep-25) -> 31.7 (Mar-26); strip the distributions and the operating drawdown was ~GBP 0.6m in the last half, ~2.8% of market cap annualised, with NO BORROWINGS ('The Group has no external financing') and only GBP 2.64m of leases. (5) THE LEAD RISK IS NEW AND IS THE CARRY, NOT THE CASH: on 2026-06-17 the dividend policy changed from a fixed pence figure to 'dividends paid as a percentage of free cash flow', and AR25 concedes the 3.25p 'is currently not covered by the year's profits'. H1 FY26 operating cash flow was GBP 1,035k against GBP 1.6m capex — H1 FCF was NEGATIVE. An FCF-linked payout implies ~1.3-2.6p, a 20-60% cut. Worse, OMG pays a SINGLE ANNUAL FINAL, no interim; the last was paid 2026-03-27 and the next relates to the 15-month FY26 whose accounts are due by 2027-06-30 — the next cheque is ~15-18 months away. The 8.98% headline is not collectible. (6) THE BEST NUMBER IN THE FILE: Motion Capture ORDER INTAKE rose 21% to GBP 34.8m in FY25. The FY25 revenue fall (-17%) was opening-order-book normalisation — 'FY24 benefited from an unusually high opening order-book of GBP 11.5m... reduced to GBP 1.0m at the start of FY25'. H1 FY26 Motion Capture then grew +10% to GBP 16.3m on wins in Eastern Europe, Japan and India. The leading indicator turned before the lagging one. (7) THE ACQUIRED ARM IS THE DRAG, NOT THE ENGINE: Vision Metrology -17% to GBP 4.4m in H1; the Sempre earn-out targets were NOT met (GBP 480k contingent consideration written to nil); goodwill headroom is thin (IVS GBP 2.7m, Sempre GBP 1.9m) and is an auditor KEY AUDIT MATTER. Management's stated plan is to double revenue partly through 'INORGANIC activities' — the GENL pathology in embryo, differing only in that OMG returned 41% of its cap at the same time. (8) 'BELOW BOOK' IS MEANINGLESS AND SLIGHTLY WORSE THAN NEUTRAL: equity GBP 60,912k less goodwill+intangibles GBP 23,504k = TANGIBLE BOOK GBP 37.4m = 33.4p/sh, BELOW the GBP 42.98m cap. The stock is at 1.15x tangible book, not 0.71x book. Use net cash (26.0p/sh) and NCAV, not P/B. Clean statement: you pay GBP 42.98m for GBP 31.7m of clearing-bank deposits plus a business earning ~GBP 2.2m adjusted — ~GBP 13.9m EV for the operating company, ~6x pre-tax owner earnings. (9) QUALITY-OF-EARNINGS FLAG: FY25 adjusting items GBP 2,605k = 5.8% of revenue and 1.18x the adjusted profit itself, and two add-backs are real economic costs — GBP 798k of acquired-intangible amortisation and GBP 750k impairment of Markerless capitalised development 'due to technical obsolescence'. Capitalised development runs GBP 3.3m/yr, 7.4% of sales. (10) GUIDANCE ARITHMETIC IS A REVIEW FLAG: 'revenue for the 15-month period expected to be approximately GBP 56m' = GBP 44.8m annualised = exactly FY25 — FLAT, despite H1 +3%. Disclosed honestly (the '15-month' is stated) but it takes arithmetic to see, and every TTM screen reads +25% growth that does not exist. ARD changed 2025-12-16, year end 30 Sep -> 31 Dec. (11) END MARKETS, HONESTLY DISCLOSED AND STABILISING: Life Sciences ~27% of revenue, and AR25 states 'a material reduction in public funding for academic spending in the United States... expected to persist'. FY25 North America -29%. But H1 FY26 US academic and entertainment 'remained broadly in line with the prior-year period' — stabilised at a lower base. No customer >10% of revenue. No profit warnings in 18 months. (12) INSIDERS BUYING INTO THE FALL: the Chair's connected person bought at 38.5p on 2026-06-29, within 1p of today's price, alongside two other PDMR dealings that fortnight. Register ~99.5% public and RETAIL-PLATFORM DOMINATED (HL 9.01 + II 7.63 + AJ Bell 3.13 + Charles Stanley 12.95 ~ 32.7%), which mechanically explains two consecutive June air-pockets on a 237bp spread. (13) PFIC, HONESTLY: the two statutory tests are DISJUNCTIVE — the house 'conjunctive' language applies only to the income-test PROXY — and a publicly traded foreign corp must run the asset test at FAIR MARKET VALUE. Spot: 31.7 / (42.98 cap + ~17.5 liabs) = 52.4%, fails. But the statute uses the AVERAGE of quarterly measurement dates: on trailing averages ~49-50%, a coin flip. PFIC-MARGINAL, not determined; a +7% move to ~41p clears it. Mechanism: the de-rate manufactures the status — and capital returns are the cure for BOTH problems, since distributing cash from a numerator smaller than its denominator REDUCES the passive share (a GBP 3.7m dividend takes 52.4% to 49.3%). THE REAL ASYMMETRY vs GENL CUTS AGAINST OMG: a Sec.1296 mark-to-market election needs marketable stock on a QUALIFIED EXCHANGE. GENL is LSE Main Market — clean. OMG is AIM, where qualification is defensible but not determined. If AIM does not qualify, MTM is unavailable, QEF is unavailable in practice, and Sec.1291 applies: dividends lose qualified treatment (~54% CA vs ~37%), any distribution above 125% of the trailing 3-year average is throwback-taxed with an interest charge (so a dividend INCREASE is tax-penalised), and gain on sale loses LTCG entirely. This is the single largest reason this is a 4 and not a 6. (14) VERDICT SHAPE: DE-RATE on the operating line, DERAILMENT of the carry. e_FV 42.1p vs a 38.4p ask = +9.6pp, ~+7.2pp net of the 237bp touch, gross of tax — a fairly-paid risk with a thin edge overlay.
